indicator_definition: This indicator measures the proportion of groundwater monitoring stations where the average nitrate concentration exceeds 50 milligrams per litre (the EU threshold under the Nitrates Directive). It is expressed as a percentage of all monitored stations. Data are reported by member states under the Nitrates Directive.
rationale: Nitrate pollution of groundwater, primarily from agricultural sources, poses risks to drinking water quality and aquatic ecosystems. Reducing nitrate concentrations requires improved agricultural nutrient management. Progress means a reduction in the proportion of monitoring stations exceeding the 50 mg/l threshold.
methodology_characteristics: Data are collected by member states under Council Directive 91/676/EEC concerning the protection of waters against pollution caused by nitrates from agricultural sources (Nitrates Directive) and reported to the European Commission every four years. Eurostat compiles and publishes the data.
